newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek cash rates hold, ecu/drachma rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Greek cash rates hold, ecu/drachma rangebound.

text.p: Greek money market rates were hovering around morning levels in late calm trading, ecu/drachma was marginally higher and volume in the secondary bond market was depressed on uncertainty over tax issues, dealers said.

"Interbank rates are unmoved since this morning," said a money dealer at a foreign bank. "There are no incentives for rate moves with the central bank keeping its overnight intervention bid unchanged at 12.40 percent and most players squared."
Bond dealers said trading volume was very thin as players were uncertain about issues relating to the taxation of government securities.

Banks have yet to agree whether the 7.5 percent tax on interest earned from state securities would be reflected on clean prices or on accrual interest when banks dealt with each other. Talks on the issue are continuing.
Greece will auction 300 billion drachmas of 12-month T-bills on February 3 and issue two-year zero coupon bonds on December 31, the finance ministry said in a statement on Tuesday.
The terms of the auction of T-bills will be announced on January 30.
Some dealers said the finance ministry should have auctioned the T-bills on January 31 when there are expiries of T-bills and the banks would have an incentive to bid more aggressively.
The mark was quoted at 157.10/20 drachmas from Wedensday's 157.050 fix, the dollar at 257.92/02 drachmas from 259.630 and the Ecu at 304.32/42 from 304.400 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma is trading slightly lower than the 304.40 level seen at the fixing," said a trader. "Rangebound trading is the norm in the absence of trading factors."
